Addigy announced today the launch of its Intelligence Suite, a solution designed to address this challenge, bringing a series of new tools and control features that help IT teams strengthen compliance while enabling the use of AI tools in an IT-approved manner.

Addigy builds device management software for managed service providers and IT teams handling Apple devices, and the Intelligence Suite embeds the AI layer directly into the existing platform, rather than operating as a standalone console.

What does the Addigy Intelligence Suite include?

Addigy's AI Script Assist can write, review, and recommend operations on behalf of administrators, requiring administrator approval while adhering to customers' existing RBAC rules rather than bypassing them. The natural language reporting feature aims to let users focus on what they want to know, rather than how to build a report.

Addigy states that its AI operates entirely within Addigy's own environment, and customer data will never be transmitted to external frontier models. Every operation is processed locally, and every AI feature has security guardrails built in rather than added as an afterthought. Alongside the launch of the new Intelligence Suite, Addigy is also offering an MCP server that opens its device management control plane to AI agents, with administrator-defined guardrails for every action taken by the agents.

Addigy's new tools also address the "shadow AI" aspect, which I believe is one of the more interesting parts. Addigy has compliance rules built in by default, helping Apple IT administrators see, monitor, control, and even block various AI tools across their fleet of Macs. This directly addresses an issue I have raised many times: employees are adopting AI tools at a pace far faster than the IT department's approval process, and it is ultimately the IT team that bears the risk.

Summary

Many of the tools IT teams need in the AI era are currently being built. With any new technology, we tend to try things out within existing solutions and then adjust the tools as needed. AI applications have been around for several years now, and I'm glad to see announcements like this providing IT teams with practical tools to manage AI usage across the entire fleet, while also delivering real benefits to IT through new AI capabilities.
